speaker: Me
text: Hi Hannah, thanks for making time. I'd like to hear how your team uses analytics today, and what's missing. Is it okay if I record this for my notes?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Sure, no problem. Happy to help, we've been using your product for about eight months now.

speaker: Me
text: Great. Can you walk me through a typical week? Who looks at the data, and when?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: I run regional operations, so Monday morning is the big one. I check sales per store for the weekend, then I forward screenshots to about thirty store managers.

speaker: Me
text: Screenshots? How does that work for you?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Honestly, not great. It takes me almost an hour, and managers ask me follow-up questions because they can't filter anything. I'd love a weekly email with a PDF or a spreadsheet per store.

speaker: Me
text: That's helpful. What would the report need to contain for the managers to actually use it?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Revenue against last week and last year, top ten products, and stock-outs. If it showed the comparison against the regional average, that would be the cherry on top.

speaker: Me
text: And what format do the managers prefer? PDF, Excel?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Most of them read on their phones, so PDF. But the finance team would want Excel to merge it with their own numbers.

speaker: Me
text: Understood. Where does your data live? Is it in a warehouse?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Our central data team moved everything to Snowflake in the summer. Right now we upload CSV files every night, which breaks about once a month.

speaker: Me
text: So a direct Snowflake connection would remove that upload step.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Exactly. Our data team would be very happy. They told me they won't renew a tool that still needs manual uploads next year.

speaker: Me
text: That's a clear signal, thank you. What about security? Single sign-on?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: IT requires SAML for everything new from January. We got an exception for you until March, but not longer.

speaker: Me
text: Good to know, that's a deadline we can plan against.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: I've also looked at the dashboard editor. Some managers wanted to build their own views, but it's too complicated for them.

speaker: Me
text: What would simple look like to them? Pick a store, pick a metric, done?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Yes, basically. Templates they can just open and change the store. They don't want to think about queries.

speaker: Me
text: If we could deliver weekly exports in January, would you roll them out to all thirty stores right away?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: I'd pilot with five stores for two weeks, then everyone. If it works, I can probably get budget for more seats too.

speaker: Me
text: That would be great. Could you send me an example of the screenshot you send today?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Sure, I'll send one of last week's right after this call.

speaker: Me
text: And I'll come back to you with a prototype of the weekly report before Christmas, so you can react to something concrete.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Perfect. Thanks for asking, it's rare that vendors actually listen.

speaker: Me
text: Thank you, Hannah. Talk soon.
